name: Fitch AEO
author: fitchaeocheck

sections.description:
Fitch AEO is the official plugin of Fitch Technologies LLC (fitchtechnologies.com), the developer of the Fitch AEO service and the Fitch AEO Check browser extension. It is not affiliated with Fitch Ratings or Fitch Group.

Fitch AEO scores pages for AI search readiness and plans fixes. This plugin lets the Fitch AEO service implement those fixes on your site safely:

  • Staged, not live. Proposed changes are stored in the plugin’s own table. Nothing on your live pages changes when a fix is staged.
  • Private preview. Each batch of staged changes gets a signed preview link that expires after seven days. Preview pages are sent with noindex, nofollow and no-cache headers and show a visible “Fitch AEO preview” bar.
  • Apply after approval. A change is applied only when a person approves it in their Fitch AEO account. Before writing, the plugin checks that the field has not been edited since the change was staged; if it has, nothing is written.
  • One-step rollback. Any applied change can be reverted. If the field was edited after the change was applied, the plugin refuses and shows the original, the applied and the current value, unless an override is explicitly requested.
  • Least privilege. Post changes need the Editor role. Site-wide changes need one extra permission, fitch_aeo_site, which an Administrator grants to the dedicated Fitch AEO user from Settings > Fitch AEO.

Version 1.0.0 supports post titles, content, excerpts, meta titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs and JSON-LD structured data on posts and pages, plus two site-wide fixes: rules added to the robots.txt that WordPress generates, and an llms.txt file served at /llms.txt. When no SEO plugin is active, the plugin prints applied meta titles, descriptions, canonical links and JSON-LD itself. With Yoast SEO (28 or later), Rank Math or All in One SEO (5 or later) active, meta titles, descriptions and canonical URLs are written into that SEO plugin’s own fields, so you see and can edit them there, and they stay if you remove this plugin; JSON-LD is added to that plugin’s own structured data, never as a second script. Values containing the SEO plugin’s template variables, and structured data of a type it already prints (WebSite, WebPage, Organization, BreadcrumbList), are refused. Older versions of those SEO plugins are refused as before. If your site has a physical robots.txt or llms.txt file in the WordPress folder, the matching site-wide fix is refused, because your web server serves that file instead. robots.txt rules are also refused while the site discourages search engines (Settings > Reading), and llms.txt is refused on sites with plain permalinks. Body content on page builder pages is never written automatically.

External services

This plugin is the WordPress side of the Fitch AEO service, operated by Fitch Technologies LLC. The plugin itself never sends requests to that service or to any other server. The service connects to your site:

  • What it is: Fitch AEO scores pages for AI search readiness and plans fixes. With your approval, it stages and applies those fixes through this plugin’s REST routes.
  • When: only after you create an Application Password for a dedicated user and enter it on your Fitch AEO account page, and only while that password is valid.
  • What it sends and reads: proposed field values (titles, descriptions, canonical URLs, JSON-LD, robots.txt rules, llms.txt); the plugin, WordPress and PHP versions; which SEO plugin and page builders are active; and the current values of the fields it is asked to change.
  • Terms of service: https://fitchtechnologies.com/aeo/terms/
  • Privacy and data retention: https://fitchtechnologies.com/aeo/privacy/

Service

This plugin is the WordPress side of the Fitch AEO service operated by Fitch Technologies LLC (https://fitchtechnologies.com/). The service connects to your site’s REST API (/wp-json/fitch-aeo/v1) using an Application Password that you create for a dedicated user and enter on your Fitch AEO account page. You can revoke that Application Password at any time from the user’s profile screen, which immediately cuts off access.

Privacy

The plugin makes no outbound HTTP requests. It never contacts Fitch Technologies or any other server. All traffic is initiated by the Fitch AEO service calling your site with the credential you created.

What the plugin stores on your site:

  • A table {prefix}fitch_aeo_changes holding each staged change: the object and field it targets, the value before the change, the proposed value, SHA-256 digests of both, its status, the WordPress user id that staged it and timestamps.
  • A random per-site preview secret in the option fitch_aeo_preview_secret, used only to sign preview links. It is generated on your site and never sent anywhere.
  • Post meta _fitch_aeo_meta_title, _fitch_aeo_meta_description and _fitch_aeo_canonical_url on posts and pages where such a change has been applied while no SEO plugin is active, and _fitch_aeo_schema_jsonld wherever JSON-LD has been applied. They are stored on your site, shown on your public pages as the page title, meta description, Open Graph tags, canonical link and JSON-LD, and are not exposed through the core WordPress REST API.
  • With Yoast SEO, Rank Math or All in One SEO active, applied meta titles, descriptions and canonical URLs are stored in that plugin’s own fields instead, exactly as if you had typed them there, and stay after this plugin is removed.
  • The plugin-owned options fitch_aeo_robots_rules (added to your public robots.txt) and fitch_aeo_llms_txt (served publicly at /llms.txt) once a site-level change is applied, and fitch_aeo_db_version. Older versions could also store fitch_aeo_schema, which uninstall still removes.
  • The fitch_aeo_site permission on the users an Administrator grants it to.

What the Fitch AEO service reads through the plugin: the plugin, WordPress and PHP versions, which SEO plugin and page builders are active, whether physical robots.txt and llms.txt files exist, and the current values of the fields it is asked to change. The service’s own data handling is described in the Fitch AEO privacy policy and data retention policy on fitchtechnologies.com.

The plugin sets no cookies and collects no visitor data. Preview links are capability URLs: anyone holding a link can see that batch’s staged content until it expires or the batch is discarded.

Uninstalling the plugin (Plugins > Delete) removes its table, its options, its post meta and the fitch_aeo_site permission from every user. Title, content and excerpt changes that were already applied to your posts stay in place, as normal post edits; meta titles, descriptions, canonical links, JSON-LD, robots.txt rules and llms.txt set by the plugin stop being served. Deactivating the plugin also stops serving /llms.txt.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin zip from Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin and activate it.
  2. Create a user named fitch-aeo with the Editor role.
  3. Optional, for site-wide fixes: in Settings > Fitch AEO, grant the site-level permission to that user.
  4. On that user’s profile screen, create an Application Password named “Fitch AEO” and enter it, with the site URL and username, on your Fitch AEO account page. Never paste it into a chat.
sections.faq:
I use Yoast SEO, Rank Math or All in One SEO. Will titles be printed twice?

No. While Yoast SEO (28 or later), Rank Math or All in One SEO (5 or later) is active, Fitch AEO prints no title, description, Open Graph or canonical tags of its own. It writes approved meta titles, descriptions and canonical URLs into that SEO plugin’s own fields, and the SEO plugin prints them. Older versions of those SEO plugins are not supported, so meta title, description and canonical changes are refused while one is active.

With no SEO plugin active, on WordPress 6.9 and later the plugin adds its description and Open Graph tags only when the page head does not already have them. On earlier WordPress versions it prints them without that check.

I already have a robots.txt or llms.txt file. What happens?

The plugin leaves it alone. A physical file in your WordPress folder is served by your web server before WordPress runs, so the plugin refuses robots.txt or llms.txt changes on that site and the Fitch AEO service gives you instructions to edit the file yourself.

Does this plugin change my pages on its own?

No. It only stores proposed changes. Changes are applied when the Fitch AEO service asks the plugin to apply a batch that a person has approved.

What happens on page builder pages?

Titles and excerpts can be changed. Body content on Elementor, Divi, WPBakery, Beaver Builder and Bricks pages is never written automatically; the service gives you instructions instead.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • Description and Open Graph tags are added through WordPress’s template enhancement output buffer (6.9 and later) instead of an output buffer opened by the plugin. Earlier WordPress versions print them without duplicate detection.
  • Staged titles, content and excerpts shown in previews are passed through wp_kses_post(), and staged SEO values through sanitize_text_field() or esc_url_raw().
  • The readme states who publishes the plugin.
  • The FAQ now matches how meta titles and descriptions work with an SEO plugin.

1.0.0

  • First public release on WordPress.org. Same features as 0.4.0.
  • Tested up to WordPress 7.1 (end to end in CI on 7.1.4 with Yoast SEO 28.8, Rank Math 1.0.281 and All in One SEO 5.0.5).
  • The readme documents the Fitch AEO service under External services.
  • Plugin renamed “Fitch AEO” for the WordPress.org directory. Every PHP file now exits when loaded outside WordPress.

0.4.0

  • Meta titles, descriptions and canonical URLs are written into Yoast SEO (28 or later), Rank Math or All in One SEO (5 or later) when one is active, and read back after every write. Verified end to end on Yoast SEO 28.8, Rank Math 1.0.281 and All in One SEO 5.0.5.
  • JSON-LD is added to the active SEO plugin’s structured data graph through its own filter. Rank Math merges an FAQPage into its WebPage node.
  • Values with the SEO plugin’s template variables, and JSON-LD nodes of types the SEO plugin already prints, are refused.
  • Previews show staged titles, descriptions and canonical URLs through the SEO plugin’s own output (Rank Math previews show the live canonical URL; the staged one applies on publish).
  • With Yoast SEO, the post’s Yoast indexable is rebuilt after each change so the page shows it at once.

0.3.0

  • Canonical URLs (same host, https only) and JSON-LD structured data can be staged, previewed, applied and rolled back on posts and pages when no SEO plugin is active. The canonical link replaces WordPress’s own; JSON-LD is printed as one safely encoded script.
  • robots.txt rules for named crawlers are added to the robots.txt WordPress generates, in a clearly marked block.
  • llms.txt is served at /llms.txt as plain text, with noindex and nosniff headers.
  • Both site-wide fixes are refused when a physical robots.txt or llms.txt exists, and the status route lists which site fields the site accepts.
  • robots.txt rules are refused, and never printed, while Settings > Reading discourages search engines. llms.txt is refused on sites with plain permalinks, where /llms.txt cannot be served.
  • The unrendered placeholder site fields from earlier versions are replaced.

0.2.0

  • Meta titles and meta descriptions can be staged, previewed, applied and rolled back on posts and pages when no SEO plugin is active, and are printed as the document title, meta description and Open Graph tags without duplicating tags already in the page head.
  • Refused with a clear reason while Yoast SEO, Rank Math or All in One SEO is active.
  • The status route lists the post fields the site accepts.

0.1.0

  • Developer preview: REST API, staged change store, preview links, apply and rollback with conflict checks, SEO plugin and page builder detection.

screenshots.caption: Fixes are staged in the plugin's own table and shown on a private, noindexed preview link until a person approves them.
With Yoast SEO, Rank Math or All in One SEO active, titles, descriptions and canonical URLs go into that plugin's own fields, and JSON-LD joins its schema graph.
Every applied change keeps its original value. Rollback stops rather than overwrite a later edit.
